documentary.director:
THE LOOK (fixed, it is the brand): stylized realism, a feature-film previz grown up. Faceless white mannequins for
every person (never a human face), real materials and costumes, era-accurate ships, vehicles and buildings,
atmospheric light, fog and weather. Captions live in the bottom quarter of the frame: keep it free of text and of the
subject's key action.

san_andreas.director:
THE LOOK (this film's preset: SAN ANDREAS — the engine applies it to every shot on top of your look block; you never
set it and never imitate it with grades): the PlayStation 2 game look of 2004 — a soft 640x448 frame upscaled, the orange-yellow
colour filter, wide glow on bright walls and skies, a short brown-orange smog that swallows the distance, matte
plain materials, soft blob shadows. It must read as a loving recreation of that era's cutscenes, never as a broken render. Faceless mannequins for every person (never a human face, in this look too), real materials and costumes, era-accurate ships, vehicles and buildings. Captions live in the bottom quarter of the frame: keep it free of text and of the
subject's key action.
san_andreas.review: THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL — this film uses the SAN ANDREAS (PS2-era game look) preset: the soft low-resolution image, the orange colour filter, the glow on bright surfaces, the short orange smog and the matte, plain materials. That is the look: do not score it as blurry, dark, blown, cheap or low-detail, and do not fix it back toward realism (no grade, exposure, fog or camera changes against the look). Judge craft INSIDE the look: the story, the subject reading at a glance, the motion, the hard fails H1-H8 (all still apply), faceless mannequins. Flag a hero lost in the smog (keep it within ~60 m).
san_andreas.qa: THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL: SAN ANDREAS (the PS2-era game look) — soft, low-resolution, orange-filtered, glowing, smoggy, plain materials. Never flag the look itself as blurry, dark or cheap; flag only what is wrong inside it. Flag a hero lost in the smog.
san_andreas.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET san_andreas (this film) — stage it like the game's cutscenes and missions: daylight (morning, afternoon,
golden; dusk and night for the night missions — the smog thins after dark), streets, cars, houses, the block, the
desert road; tripod-like framings, slow push_in, low angles, a behind-the-car chase (follow, tracking_low), a slow
crane over the block. Keep the hero within ~60 m: the smog eats the distance. No FPV skims through foliage, no
macro inserts of materials (the soft frame has no fine detail). look.grade stays the story clock (warm / cold).

noir.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET noir (this film) — light it like a 1940s crime picture: night, dusk and interiors first (a street under
lamps, a room lit by one practical: a desk lamp, a window, headlights); one strong key from the side or above, deep
shadow everywhere else; low angles, slow pushes, figures as silhouettes against a lit window or a streetlamp, haze
0.6-0.8 and a little fog for smoke. The colour is gone, so the story lives in light and shadow: the hero must still
separate (a rim, a lit background behind a dark figure).

diorama.director:

diorama.review: THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL — this film uses the DIORAMA (tilt-shift miniature) preset: the blur above and below the focus band, the saturated toy colours and the stepped (on twos) motion of the world. That is the look: do not score it as blurry, dark, blown, cheap or low-detail, and do not fix it back toward realism (no grade, exposure, fog or camera changes against the look). Judge craft INSIDE the look: the story, the subject reading at a glance, the motion, the hard fails H1-H8 (all still apply), faceless mannequins. Flag a hero that falls outside the sharp band, and an eye-level shot (the miniature needs height).
diorama.qa: THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL: DIORAMA (tilt-shift miniature) — a sharp band through the middle, blur above and below, toy colours, the world moving on twos. Never flag the look itself as blurry, dark or cheap; flag only what is wrong inside it. Flag a hero outside the sharp band.
diorama.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET diorama (this film) — the miniature only reads from ABOVE: look 35-60 degrees down (flyover_high,
crane_down, orbit, keys) from 30-150 m, fov 24-34, the hero across the MIDDLE of the frame (the sharp band is the
central ~12 % of the frame height; the blur grows above and below): towns, ports, roads, battlefields, convoys,
crowds. Bright daylight (morning, noon, afternoon; clear or scattered). No eye-level or FPV shots (no miniature,
everything blurs), no night. Labels stay sharp.

cel.director:
THE LOOK (this film's preset: CEL — the engine applies it to every shot on top of your look block; you never
set it and never imitate it with grades): a cel-shaded graphic novel — the light in two hard steps, flat colour fields, bold black ink
outlines on every figure, vehicle and building (never on grass or trees), the ground and plants painted in a few flat
tones behind them, no shine, no grain, no motion blur. Faceless mannequins for every person (never a human face, in this look too), real materials and costumes, era-accurate ships, vehicles and buildings. Captions live in the bottom quarter of the frame: keep it free of text and of the
subject's key action.
cel.review: THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL — this film uses the CEL (cel-shaded graphic novel) preset: flat colours, light in hard steps, black outlines on the figures, vehicles and buildings, and a ground and plants painted in a few flat tones (no fine texture). That is the look: do not score it as blurry, dark, blown, cheap or low-detail, and do not fix it back toward realism (no grade, exposure, fog or camera changes against the look). Judge craft INSIDE the look: the story, the subject reading at a glance, the motion, the hard fails H1-H8 (all still apply), faceless mannequins. Flag a subject without its outline (merged into a same-depth neighbour) and outlines that break into noise.
cel.qa: THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL: CEL (cel-shaded graphic novel) — flat colours, hard light steps, black outlines on figures, vehicles and buildings, a flat painted ground. Never flag the look itself as blurry, dark or cheap; flag only what is wrong inside it. Flag outline noise.
cel.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET cel (this film) — draw every shot like a graphic-novel panel: bold silhouettes against simple
backgrounds (the ink outlines figures, vehicles, buildings and props by depth and by their creases: a figure in front of a
wall, the ground or the sky outlines cleanly; the ground, grass and trees are painted flat, never inked), one clear key light (morning, afternoon, golden; night with practicals) that throws strong
shadow shapes, medium and close scales for people, dynamic low or high angles, few objects per shot. No tall grass
or foliage in front of the hero (it hides the outline), no thick fog (it erases the outlines).

clay_lite.review: THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL — this film uses the CLAY (stop-motion) preset: plasticine surfaces (lumps, thumb smudges, a waxy sheen), putty puppets, a soft simplified ground, soft warm light, a shallow miniature focus and the stepped (on twos) motion of the world. That is the look: do not score it as blurry, dark, blown, cheap or low-detail, and do not fix it back toward realism (no grade, exposure, fog or camera changes against the look). clay_lite.qa: THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL: CLAY (stop-motion) — plasticine materials (lumps, smudges), putty puppets, a soft ground, soft warm light, shallow focus, the world on twos. Never flag the look itself as blurry, dark or cheap; flag only what is wrong inside it. Never flag the stepped motion.
clay_lite.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET clay_lite (this film) — stage it like a stop-motion set: small worlds (a room, a street corner, a field
with a few props), medium and close scales, a locked-off or slowly gliding camera (push_in, orbit slow, keys with 2-3
keys), warm interiors and soft daylight (morning, afternoon, golden; overcast works), few characters with clear
poses and actions. No FPV, no huge vistas, no extreme speed.

hologram.review: THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL — this film uses the HOLOGRAM (cyan projection on a black void) preset: the monochrome cyan, the black sky and distance, the ground and plants sunk into the dark, the glowing edges and rim light and the scanlines. That is the look: do not score it as blurry, dark, blown, cheap or low-detail, and do not fix it back toward realism (no grade, exposure, fog or camera changes against the look). hologram.qa: THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL: HOLOGRAM — cyan monochrome on a black void, glowing outlines, scanlines. Never flag the look itself as blurry, dark or cheap; flag only what is wrong inside it. Flag a subject lost in the void.
hologram.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET hologram (this film) — every shot is an evidence-room projection: one isolated subject (a building, a
vehicle, a device, a ship, a figure, a globe) close enough to fill the frame (the void swallows anything past
~200 m), orbit, slow push_in and reveal_rise around it, the ground and plants vanish into the void, so the subject is always a figure, vehicle, building, device
or prop; any time of day (the sky is always black, the key light still shapes the object); labels for names and
numbers.

game.director:
THE LOOK (this film's preset: GAME — QUEST, the 3D video game; the engine applies it to every shot on top of your look block;
you never set it): history PLAYED as a bright 3D video game. The viewer is the hero ("you") and levels up. Every person is a
CHIBI TOY FIGURE WITH A FACE (a big round head, dot eyes, blush, a button nose; this look is the ONE exception to "faceless"):
the engine builds every cast member, every `figure.*` crowd and every `figure.person` as chibi figures automatically, so
stage people exactly as usual. The world is a low-poly toy world: always `"world": {"biome": "game_meadow"}` (or game_autumn,
game_desert, game_snow, game_beach, game_volcano, game_moon — the place's climate), daylight (morning, noon, afternoon,
golden; dusk or night only when the story is at night). Use the game kinds (game.*) for everything they cover: level pads
and the level map, chests and coins, rings and trophies, the golden gate, tents and camps, roads, columns, temples, walls,
houses, castles, towers, standards, beams and level-up bursts, world tags (YOU ▼, name plates, danger bars, selection
boxes). Legion draws a game HUD on top of every frame (a level badge top-left, stat bars top-right, a 6-slot hotbar at
the bottom centre): keep the hero and the key action in the middle band of the frame — never in the top 15 % corners or
behind the bottom-centre hotbar — and put no story text of your own in those zones. No captions are burnt in.
game.review:
THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL (it overrides every "faceless" / "faces at all" / "a mannequin with a face" rule of the rubric and of QUALITY.md: in this look the people are chibi figures and their FACES ARE REQUIRED) — this film uses the GAME (QUEST, 3D video game) preset: chibi toy figures WITH faces (big heads,
dot eyes, blush), a bright saturated low-poly toy world, puffy cartoon clouds, shiny chrome and gold, world-space game tags.
That is the look: never score the faces, the cartoon proportions, the toy colours or the low-poly facets as cheap or wrong,
and never fix them toward realism. Judge it as a premium game trailer: the hero reads at a glance and looks the same in every
shot of the same level (his outfit changes ONLY at a level-up), the game devices (level-up burst, chest, ring, gate,
formation, selection box, tags) land on their words, the camera moves like a game camera (smooth follow, orbit, push-in,
crane, top-down), the frame keeps the HUD zones clear (top corners, bottom centre). The hard fails H1-H8 still apply.
game.qa:
THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL (it overrides the "mannequin with a face" flag: chibi faces are required here): GAME (QUEST) — chibi toy figures with faces, a bright low-poly toy world, cartoon
clouds, game tags. Never flag the look itself (faces, proportions, toy colours, facets) as cheap; flag what is wrong inside it:
a hero whose outfit changes inside a level, a figure inside a prop, an empty or static shot, the subject hidden in the
top corners or behind the bottom-centre hotbar, a wrong or missing object the words name.
game.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET game (QUEST, this film) — a level-up video game. How to stage it:
- THE HERO: one CastDef per LEVEL, all with the same face: copy the ids, kits and `chibi` blocks given in THE SCRIPT WRITER'S
  NOTES exactly (hero_l1, hero_l2, ...); use the ref of the level being narrated. The hero's face always shows (never a
  great_helm on the hero); film it: most hero shots are close or medium, facing the camera or three-quarter. A CastDef's `chibi` block:
  {"outfit": tunic|armor_bands|mail|plate|cuirass|robe|toga|coat|uniform|suit|dress|shirt|apron|spacesuit|labcoat|kimono|samurai|rags|fur,
   "top": "#hex|red|navy|white|...", "legs": "#hex", "skirt_color": "#hex", "accent": "#hex", "trim": "#hex", "metal": "#hex",
   "wear": galea|nasal_helm|kettle|great_helm|crown|laurel|hood|nemes|kabuto|stahlhelm|m1|brodie|hard_hat|shako|kepi|top_hat|bowler|fedora|cowboy|straw|pith|tricorn|bicorne|turban|fez|beret|cap|bandana|headband|wizard|chef|mitre|bubble|none,
   "crest": none|transverse|long, "crest_color": "#hex", "cape": "#hex", "tabard": "#hex", "sash": "#hex", "stripe": "#hex", "medals": true,
   "held": gladius|sword|longsword|katana|spear|pilum|trident|pitchfork|staff|vine_stick|torch|flag|standard|aquila|hammer|pickaxe|axe|shovel|sickle|scroll|book|lantern|bag|coin_bag|musket|rifle|pistol|bow|quill|cup|briefcase|phone,
   "held_l": scutum|round_shield|parma|buckler|hoplon|heater|kite|book|lantern|scroll|torch,
   "back": furca|backpack|quiver|oxygen, "hair": curly|short|side|spiky|long|ponytail|bun|braids|topknot|afro|bald, "hair_color": brown|dark|black|blond|ginger|grey|white|#hex,
   "beard": none|mustache|full|long, "skin": light|fair|medium|tan|brown|dark, "expression": neutral|happy|determined|worried|angry|surprised|sad,
   "glasses": true, "height": 1.3-1.7}
- ACTIONS (cast, game.npc, game.formation): stand ride walk march run salute point wave cheer celebrate levelup dig build swing
  block talk nod look_around think carry sit kneel bow scared tired aim read count pray push fall lie. `ride` puts the cast
  member on a chibi horse (path + speed: walk 1.6, trot 3, gallop 6 m/s); a riderless horse is game.horse. `levelup` = a hop and
  a full turn with the arms up (1.1 s) — the level-up beat. Moving actions walk `path` [[x, z], ...] at `speed`.
- CAMERA: chibis are 1.45 m tall with the face at ~1.1 m. Close and medium shots are `keys` at 0.9-1.6 m with
  `"limits": "macro"` (fov 30-42), 1.8-4 m from the hero, always moving (push 15-30 %, arc 20-40°, or follow). Follow shots:
  keys moving with the walker 2.5-3.5 m behind / beside at 1.4-1.8 m. Wides: 8-30 m up looking 30-55° down on formations,
  camps, the map. Top-down: the level map, an army grid, a camp. Use dof on close shots (the reference blurs the background).
- THE LEVEL-UP SHOT (the first 1.5-2.5 s of every level): the hero on the stage, `"action": "levelup"` at t 0.2, a
  `game.burst` at the hero's feet (t 0.3) and a `game.beam` (t 0.1, t_out 1.6); the camera low behind or in front, pushing in;
  the HUD's LEVEL card covers the middle of the frame for ~1.2 s, so the hero's head and the burst read around it.
- GAME DEVICES (pick the one the words name): a quest = a figure doing the task (marching the road with milestones:
  game.road; digging: dig; building: game.camp with build [t0, t1] = the camp builds itself, time-lapse); a reward = game.chest
  (t_open on the word), game.coins rain, game.ring / game.trophy floating; danger = a `game.tag` danger bar over the threatened
  figure, arrows, a swing; numbers of people = game.formation (count = the number, up to 6000: 80 men = 80) or game.army
  blocks with a `game.select` box round them; rank among others = `game.tag` name plates (style name, on: ref) and `you` over
  the hero; the final level = game.gate (doors open at t_open, light pours out) with the hero walking toward it; the level
  map (game.level_map: levels n, current, progress [[t, level]], crossed [1] for a twist) as the opening and the closing image.
- Tags go in "labels": {"kind": "game.tag", "style": "you|name|danger|health|quest|count|damage|label", "text": "...",
  "on": "ref:<id>" | "groups:N" | "objects:N", "t_in": s, "t_out": s, "value": 0..1, "to": 0..1, "from": n, "count_to": n,
  "t_count": s, "unit": "..."}; {"kind": "game.select", "on": "groups:N", "t_in": s}.
- Sets: game.tent, game.camp {size, rows, cols, build}, game.road {from, to, width, milestones}, game.column, game.temple,
  game.wall {from, to}, game.house {style roman|medieval|village|modern|hut|igloo|japanese}, game.castle, game.tower,
  game.post, game.standard {style aquila|banner|flag}, game.horse {color, caparison, gait, rider}, game.campfire, game.crates, game.ship {style galley|sailship|longship,
  speed}, game.cart, game.sign {text}. Other kinds of the catalog (vehicles, aircraft, ships, landmarks, prop.build) are
  allowed when no game kind fits — the preset paints them toy-bright — but never `town.*` streets with realistic textures.

fern.director:
THE LOOK (this film's preset: FERN — the engine adds a fern film texture to every shot: fine clumped grain, slow gate
weave, red halation round bright lights, specks of dust, a heavy oval vignette; you never set those). YOU light and grade every
shot like fern: low-key 3D lit by ONE light you can explain (a moon rim, a slit, a window, a lamp), most of the frame near
black, silhouettes and rims instead of fill, haze and smoke in the air, everything moving. Grade PER SHOT with the colour
script: nocturne (blue night: sky, snow, free fall), dossier (sepia desk), void_red / void_blue (the black stage for menace,
a red keep_hue slit on the perpetrator, blue rims on the heroes), interior_warm (dark brown rooms), archive_bw (a 3D shot
imitating newsreel). Red = the perpetrator and death, blue = the heroes and night, amber = home. Faceless mannequins for every person (never a human face, in this look too), real materials and costumes, era-accurate ships, vehicles and buildings. Captions live in the bottom quarter of the frame: keep it free of text and of the
subject's key action.
fern.review: THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL — this film uses the FERN preset: low-key, mostly near-black frames lit by one motivated light (a slit, a rim, a window), film grain, dust specks, gate weave, a heavy vignette, per-shot colour (blue night, sepia desk, a red slit in a black void). That is the look: do not score it as dark, grainy, dirty, cheap or low-detail, and do not fix it back toward bright realism (no exposure, fill-light or grade changes against the look). Judge craft INSIDE the look: the story, the subject reading at a glance BY ITS LIGHT (a lit slit, a rim, a silhouette against a lighter background reads), the motion (>= 2 moving layers: subject + smoke / dust / light), the hard fails H1-H8, faceless mannequins, no lit mannequin face closer than 1 m. Flag darkness only when the subject the words name cannot be seen at all.
fern.qa: THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL: FERN — low-key, mostly black frames, one motivated light, film grain and dust. Never flag the look itself as dark, grainy or cheap; flag only what is wrong inside it. Flag dark only when the named subject cannot be seen (a rim or a lit slit reads).
fern.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET fern (this film) — the colour script per shot: nocturne for the sky / snow / night exteriors (moon
behind the subject: rim light; fog 0.1-0.2, snow or dust as the second moving layer), dossier for the desk and documents,
stage.void (a halo glow from frame 1 + a backdrop keyed up on the beat + a drifting fog.volume) + light.spot slit (colour
slit, keep_hue, spill 0.28, grade void_blue) for the antagonist, light.rig blue rims for the heroes (pistols in profile),
blinds / window cookies for rooms (light.spot beam 0.5-0.7 through haze), interior_warm with one practical lamp. Hard
pivots: transition negative (0.15 s). Keep fern's restraint: one light, slow pushes, one wow move per 20-30 s.

nocturne.director:
THE LOOK (this film's preset: NOCTURNE — the engine renders every shot in fern's blue night duotone: navy blacks, moon-blue
highlights, film grain, gate weave, soft bloom, a heavy oval vignette; you never set it and never imitate it with grades):
light it like a moonlit night — the moon or one cool light BEHIND the subject (rim light), silhouettes, haze, snow or dust
in the air. A light with keep_hue true (a red slit, a red jump light) keeps its colour inside the blue. Faceless mannequins for every person (never a human face, in this look too), real materials and costumes, era-accurate ships, vehicles and buildings. Captions live in the bottom quarter of the frame: keep it free of text and of the
subject's key action.
nocturne.review: THE LOOK IS INTENTIONAL — this film uses the NOCTURNE (blue night duotone) preset: every shot blue-monochrome, dark, silhouettes with cool rims, grain and a heavy vignette; only keep_hue lights (red) keep their colour. That is the look: do not score it as dark, monochrome, grainy or cheap, and do not fix it back toward colour or brightness. Judge craft INSIDE the look: the story, the subject reading by its rim / silhouette, the motion, the hard fails H1-H8, faceless mannequins. Flag darkness only when the named subject cannot be seen at all.
nocturne.qa: THE LOOK OF THIS FILM IS INTENTIONAL: NOCTURNE — blue monochrome night, silhouettes, grain. Never flag the look itself as dark, blue or grainy; flag only what is wrong inside it. Flag dark only when the named subject cannot be seen.
nocturne.cookbook:
LOOK PRESET nocturne (this film) — night, dusk and dark interiors; one cool key from behind (the moon, a window, a
hatch) so every figure has a rim; haze 0.5-0.8, fog 0.1-0.3, snow or dust as the second moving layer; red keep_hue lights
(a slit, a jump light, a burning window) are the only colour: use them for danger.
